items.title: Charlie De Vore Interview, 1962-07-04
items.q: And we were playing and Doc Evans came up to me and said, gee, why don't you play a little bit more off the beat?

ctx.x: That is, that's where most white, like, for instance, the Blue Water School, the West Coast School of traditional jazz, that all seemed to me to be something they missed. They all came down to beat at the same time. The tonality was there, I always liked Lou Waters playing. He seemed to get a hot tone, but when he, his phrasing always sounded stiff to me because they were always going plump, plump, plump right on the beat. And all the good guys, the guys that I've admired the most and to me that play the most…
you were coming down right on the beat.
